verdicts.statement: The East German government built the Berlin Wall in 1961.
verdicts.reason: The context states that East Germany constructed the Wall starting on 13 August 1961.

verdicts.statement: The Berlin Wall was built to prevent citizens of East Germany from emigrating or fleeing to West Berlin.
verdicts.reason: The context identifies preventing East Germans from entering or fleeing to West Berlin as the main purpose believed by most people and states that the Wall prevented almost all such emigration.

verdicts.statement: Before the construction of the Berlin Wall, about 3.5 million East Germans had circumvented emigration restrictions.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that 3.5 million East Germans circumvented Eastern Bloc emigration restrictions before the Wall was erected.

verdicts.statement: A large number of East Germans circumvented emigration restrictions by crossing from East Berlin into West Berlin.
verdicts.reason: The context states that many of the 3.5 million East Germans who circumvented emigration restrictions crossed from East Berlin into West Berlin.

verdicts.statement: The East German government officially described the Berlin Wall as an “anti-fascist protective rampart.”
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly gives anti-fascist protective rampart as the East German government description of the Wall.

verdicts.statement: The East German government claimed the Berlin Wall was intended to deter aggression from the West.
verdicts.reason: The context explicitly states that the government claimed the Wall was intended to dissuade aggression from the West.

verdicts.statement: The East German government claimed the Berlin Wall was needed because of Western agents.
verdicts.reason: The context identifies the activities of Western agents in Eastern Europe as another official justification for the Wall.

verdicts.statement: The East German government claimed the Berlin Wall was needed because West Berliners were buying subsidized goods in East Berlin.
verdicts.reason: The context lists the government claim that West Berliners were buying out state-subsidized goods in East Berlin among its justifications for the Wall.

verdicts.statement: The official East German explanations for the construction of the Berlin Wall were widely met with skepticism.
verdicts.reason: The context states that East Germans and others greeted these official statements with skepticism.
